newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan welcomes Fujimori's Cuban plan on siege.
newsitem.headline: Japan welcomes Fujimori's Cuban plan on siege.

text.p: Japan welcomes Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori's plan to seek Cuba's help in accepting the Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, a top government spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We highly appreciate President Fujimori's initiatives and we think this is a very effective method of resolving the crisis," Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a regular news conference.
In Havana, Fujimori told a news conference that Cuba was willing to accept the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels for asylum.
Kajiyama said both the Peruvian and Japanese governments must formally request the Cuban government to make such an arrangement.
"I will not say whether this is morally right or wrong," Kajiyama said. "I think it is an effective way both in terms of not giving in to terrorism and of ending this peacefully."
The MRTA rebels have been holding 72 VIP hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence since December 17.
